text: Paper · NeurIPS 2020 · arXiv 2005.11401 Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (RAG) Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Küttler, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Tim Rocktäschel, Sebastian Riedel, Douwe Kiela Facebook AI Research; University College London; New York University · May 2020 (arXiv v1, 22 May 2020); v4 April 2021; published at NeurIPS 2020 In one line: Coined RAG: a DPR retriever and a BART generator trained end to end, the retrieved documents treated as a latent variable and marginalised (RAG-Sequence against RAG-Token); state of the art on open-domain QA, and knowledge updated by swapping the index, not the weights.

text: Problem §1 Introduction By 2020, pretrained language models demonstrably stored facts in their parameters (GPT-2, T5): T5 fine-tuned to answer with no documents, "closed-book", was competitive with retrieval systems ( Roberts et al.
label: core

text: But parametric knowledge has three structural flaws ( §1 ): It cannot be inspected : no provenance for why the model said something, and "hallucinations".
label: core

text: It cannot be updated without retraining : the world changes, the weights do not.

text: Idea: two memories, one probabilistic model Figure 1, §2 RAG treats the retrieved document as a latent variable in a probabilistic seq2seq model and trains retriever and generator jointly, end to end, with no supervision on which document to retrieve ( §2 , §2.4 ).

text: Retriever and generator §2.2, §2.3, §3 Retriever: DPR. p η ( z | x ) is DPR , a bi-encoder of two BERT-base networks ( §2.2 ): p η ( z | x ) ∝ exp( d ( z ) ⊤ q ( x )), d ( z ) = BERT d ( z ), q ( x ) = BERT q ( x ) The top k by this score is a Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS), solved approximately in sub-linear time.

text: The dominant pattern since 2023: embed the query with an off-the-shelf embedding model, run approximate nearest-neighbour search in a vector database, concatenate the top- k chunks into the prompt of a frozen instruction-tuned LLM, generate.
label: core

text: No marginalisation (the LLM attends over all chunks at once, closer to Fusion-in-Decoder than to RAG-Token), no gradient into the retriever, no joint objective; In-Context RALM names it: "prepending grounding documents to the input, without any further training of the LM".
label: core

text: Why the shift: in-context learning got strong enough that concatenation works without fine-tuning, frontier LLMs are frozen behind APIs, and a pipeline you rebuild by re-chunking a document base is far simpler to run than co-training a retriever and a generator.
label: core
key: why the shift: in-context learning got

text: The end-to-end idea survives in research descendants (REALM before it; FiD , RETRO and Atlas after, and REPLUG , which trains only the retriever from a frozen LM's likelihoods), while the deployed world runs the frozen version.
label: core
key: the end-to-end idea survives in research

text: What did survive is most of the paper : dense bi-encoder retrieval over chunked passages (DPR's BERT bi-encoder is the ancestor of every modern embedding model); fixed, roughly 100-word chunking into a searchable index; MIPS and approximate nearest-neighbour search as the retrieval primitive (FAISS then, dedicated vector databases now); grounding to reduce hallucination and give provenance; and the killer operational argument, update knowledge by updating the index, not the weights.
label: core

text: The modern stack (embeddings, vector database, chunking, rerankers, and onwards to agentic RAG and GraphRAG ) is this architecture with the learning removed and the engineering scaled up; the Gao et al. survey 's Naive, Advanced and Modular RAG is the usual map.
label: core

text: For open-domain QA it also settled an argument of its moment: one general retrieve-and-generate recipe beat both closed-book giants (T5-11B has 11 billion trainable parameters against RAG's 516M trained; the closest-sized T5, T5-large at 770M, scores 28.9 on NQ, Appendix G ) and specialised extractive pipelines, across four benchmarks, clearly on two.
